rites.name: Merasamira
rites.text: Merasamira is a concept of Halurdock in the Singing, the undated sounding when the first roots of the world condense out of resonant silence. It is less a being than a chord that holds the young stars in tune while the deep roots set.

rites.name: Vanataala
rites.text: Vanataala is the concept of threshold-keeping in Halurdock, the idea that every door between worlds must be both opened and held shut by a bargain. In the Courts of the Age of Sundering, it was the principle invoked whenever landfall severed an old bond and a new covenant had to be sworn in its place.

rites.name: Elimeth
rites.text: Elimeth is the concept of Halurdock's Seeding, the age when the makers sow the Weave and the quiet powers lie dormant beneath the stars. It is not an event one can watch unfold, but a standing principle of stillness that the Stellar Realm holds until the first threads take root.

rites.name: Osuvauta
rites.text: Osuvauta is the concept of the Seeding in Halurdock, the quiet span when the makers plant the Weave and the powers lie dormant beneath the stars. It names the hush before any power wakes, and the stillness that the first Record keeps.

rites.name: Serallanum
rites.text: Serallanum is the concept of the Weave as the makers planted it in the Seeding, a quiet dormant pattern meant to hold the slow powers of growing kingdoms. It is named in the old groves as the thread that keeps the first sovereign's gardens from unraveling.

rites.name: Iloralira
rites.text: Iloralira is the concept of the walls that held Halurdock through its Walled Age, the belief that a boundary is a promise kept by those who build and tend it. Its orders and first crossings are remembered as acts of shaping rather than conquest, and its churches teach that every gate must be opened by someone who remembers why it was closed.

rites.name: Amerus
rites.text: Amerus is the concept of a shelved future in Halurdock, a branch of the Three Futures that the Library catalogues but never opens. During the Holy Age, when temples and orders kept their fires lit, Amerus was the idea that the ending could still turn aside.
